notes: WIKISOURCE: la.wikisource.org has no local copyright page ('Vicifons:Imperium publicum' = 404). Every page footer states that text may be used under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike License, linking to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ and to https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Policy:Terms_of_Use (both HTTP 200). The ancient/medieval texts themselves are public domain; only the transcription/formatting is CC BY-SA, so hosting is allowed with attribution (link to the page + CC BY-SA 4.0). Quality flags ('textquality' 25/50/75/100%) are recorded where present; 25% pages (Boethius, Catilinarian index) are unproofread. URL pattern: https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/<Title>/<Liber_N>; titles are case-sensitive and several differ from the usual names (Vulgata Clementina; In L. Catilinam orationes; Metamorphoses (Ovidius); De philosophiae consolatione; Regula sancti Benedicti; Historia Apollonii Regis Tyri; Proslogion seu Alloquium de Dei existentia; Gesta Romanorum (Oesterley); Epitome historiæ sacræ). Every Wikisource page offers EPUB/PDF/MOBI export via the 'Download' tool in the sidebar (WsExport); direct export URLs were not tested. The MediaWiki API rate-limited anonymous requests (HTTP 429) during this session; plain page fetches with ~1 s spacing were fine. No audio on Wikisource. INTERNET ARCHIVE: direct PDF URLs follow https://archive.org/download/<identifier>/<file>.pdf and 302-redirect to a datanode (ia8xxxxx.us.archive.org / dn7xxxxx.ca|eu.archive.org); record the archive.org/download URL, not the datanode. Several HEAD requests returned transient HTTP 500 and succeeded on retry (or 206 with a Range GET). Rights are expressed per item: library scans (cdl, cornell, toronto, Google 'goog' items) usually carry 'possible-copyright-status: NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT' + 'copyright-region: US' (US-only assertion), some Google/European items carry licenseurl = CC Public Domain Mark 1.0; user uploads in booksbylanguage_latin / booksbylanguage_portuguese usually have NO rights field, or a PD mark applied by the uploader (not reliable). Brazilian PD was judged by author death year: PD-safe = Sonnenschein (1929), Nutting (1934), Gildersleeve (1924)/Lodge (1942), Lewis (1904)/Short (1886), Hale (1928)/Buck (1955, PD in Brazil from 2026-01-01), Lhomond (1794), 18th-c. Portuguese grammars; NOT PD-safe = Puer Romanus (W. H. S. Jones d. 1963 -> 2034), the 1933 Maxey/Fay readers, Julia (Reed, death unknown), Ars Latina (1946). Ritchie, Heatley, Kingdon, Reed, Maxey, Fay death years were not found.
